conversation.text:
Police: Does Xiyuan’s name have any special meaning?
Respondent: Xiyuan was born at the 23rd week of my wife’s pregnancy. Her birth weight was less than 700 grams.
Respondent: After the surgery, before my wife and Xiyuan were transferred to the intensive care unit, a nurse loudly called my name.
Respondent: Although it was only for a few brief seconds, I saw her.
Respondent: She looked so small, like a translucent Thumbelina wrapped in red tulip petals...
Respondent: I didn’t dare to breathe for a moment, afraid that she would be blown away like a dandelion seed.
Respondent: The nurse asked me if I saw clearly, but I couldn’t see anything clearly...
Respondent: Tears kept blurring my vision, preventing me from engraving her appearance into my eyes.
Respondent: After that hurried glimpse, do you know what the first thing I did was?
Respondent: Birth registration.
Respondent: I ran all the way from the hospital to the subdistrict office. Xiyuan.
Respondent: Xi as in rhinoceros, Yuan as in origin. Isn’t it a very special name?
Respondent: I hoped she would be as strong as a rhinoceros... so I gave her this name.
Respondent: I used all my strength to write her name stroke by stroke on the paper.
Respondent: I hoped that this document bearing her name:
Respondent: would become resilient roots allowing her to take deep root in this world.
Respondent: would become a huge anchor allowing her soul to moor by our side.
